patient._comment: 'patient' contains the three sections that may be exposed in the detailed patient display: presentation, answer, and clinical.

presentation._comment: The immutable patient evidence package available for triage. Panel context controls whether other sections are locked or available.
presentation.chiefComplaint: Painful blistering rash on one side
presentation.quote: I've got burning, stabbing pain and a blistery stripe along one side of my ribs. It stops at the middle and doesn't cross over. The pain started days before the rash.
presentation.triageNote: 62-year-old female with several days of burning pain followed by grouped blisters in a narrow stripe along one side of her ribs. The rash stops at the midline, with no facial or eye involvement.

answer._comment: The authoritative game answer. Explicit ESI, destination, and destination rationale are answer-bearing content; the player's assignment remains session state.
answer.destinationReason: ESI 5 is appropriate because this localized dermatomal rash without facial or eye involvement requires medication but no counted emergency resource.

clinical._comment: Display-ready clinical interpretation derived from patient.presentation. It preserves clinical meaning but must not explicitly name or identify the correct ESI level or destination; it does not participate in scoring.
clinical.summary: This patient has unilateral burning pain followed by grouped vesicles confined to a thoracic dermatome.
clinical.acuityReason: The rash stops at the midline and has no ocular, facial, disseminated, or systemic features.
keyFindings: Grouped blisters in a narrow unilateral stripe
teachingPoints: Eye or forehead involvement requires urgent ophthalmic assessment.
Antiviral benefit is greatest when treatment begins early, especially in older or immunocompromised patients.

possibleClinicalOutcome.disposition: Oral antiviral and pain treatment would usually allow discharge with skin-care, transmission, and complication precautions.

aiImageGeneration._comment: 'aiImageGeneration' is info for AI to generate the image of the patient. Most images were done with openAI gpt-image-1 using an API, not the app, in July 2026. Look for some python scripts that are used to create these images. Be sure that the anchor-image is available and is provided to the AI - otherwise the images will not be consistent.
aiImageGeneration.pose: seated, lifting the edge of her shirt to show a rash on one side of her ribs
signs: stripe of blistery rash on one side of the torso
aiImageGeneration.prompt: Softly-shaded painterly cartoon illustration in a semi-realistic Pixar/Disney style: smooth gradient shading, soft natural lighting, gentle rounded volumes, fine delicate outlines (NOT thick flat cartoon outlines), warm detailed rendering, natural realistic proportions, single character, 3/4 front view, centered, square 1:1. Match the exact painterly style, brushwork, shading, line weight, lighting, and palette of the attached reference image. Subject: a white 62-year-old woman, seated on a blue padded clinic chair. Pose: lifting the hem of her shirt slightly to show a rash along one side of her ribs. Expression: uncomfortable, wincing. Clearly visible: a stripe of red blistery rash on one side of the torso. No text, no logos.
